title: Do Digital Nomads in Malaysia and Cambodia Need a Local SIM to Pay by QR?

body_markdown:
At a[KHQR](https://moretapay.com/networks/khqr) stand in Siem Reap, the smell of grilled pork drifts over the counter while your phone, still running a foreign SIM, opens its camera to scan the code. No local SIM needed: you only need mobile data at the moment you scan, and an app that can pay into that national network. Neither network requires a local SIM card or phone number from foreign visitors. Moreta builds Moreta Pay, a wallet that lets travelers top up in their home currency and pay local QR codes in local currency, and the app needs no local bank account and no local SIM. For most nomads, a data-only eSIM is enough. A local number only matters if you sign up for a local wallet that registers you by phone.


**About the Author:**


Moreta builds Moreta Pay, a wallet that lets foreign travelers pay national QR networks across Asia and Latin America, including Malaysia's[DuitNow](https://moretapay.com/networks/duitnow) and Cambodia's KHQR. Moreta Global Inc. is a Delaware corporation, a FinCEN-registered Money Services Business, and part of Y Combinator's Summer 2024 batch.


## Why is a local SIM the wrong thing to worry about for QR payments?


Many nomads worry about the SIM because a SIM does two separate jobs, and only one of them matters at the counter.


Picture a hawker on Gurney Drive in Penang tossing char kway teow. A laminated DuitNow sticker is taped beside his wok. Your phone needs to reach a payment server for a few seconds. That takes data. Paying him does not require a Malaysian number.


- **Data:**


lets the app authorize the payment. Roaming, an eSIM, or café Wi-Fi all work.


- **Phone number:**


a sign-up identifier that some wallets use. It comes up once, at registration, and never at the stall.


## How do DuitNow QR and KHQR actually work?


Both are national QR standards built on the EMVCo QR specification. That shared format is why the SIM question disappears.


An EMVCo code works like a standard electrical socket. The layout of the data inside the code is fixed internationally, so any app built to that spec can plug in and read the merchant ID, the currency and the amount. Behind the code, the national network routes the money to the merchant's account. Your phone carrier plays no part in that route.

## Which apps let a foreigner pay by QR without a local number?


No network blocks you over a SIM. What you still have to pick is the app you pay with, and each option has its own sign-up rules.


- **Bakong Tourists (Cambodia):**


the National Bank of Cambodia's app for visitors lets you register with an email address, then top up at the airport or your hotel.


- **Moreta Pay (both):**


verifies you with a selfie and your passport. You top up in your own currency and pay DuitNow and KHQR codes from one balance.


If you use the local apps, you sign up and verify separately in each country. A nomad who splits a season between George Town and Siem Reap should count that as setup time.


## What is the best eSIM for Malaysia or Cambodia if you mainly pay by QR?


Since payment only needs data, the best eSIM for Malaysia and the best eSIM for Cambodia are simply the plans that keep you online reliably in the places you actually spend time.


- **Data-only is fine.**


An eSIM connects your phone to a local network with no need to swap SIMs or pay roaming, though what you get depends on the package


.


- **Pick regional plans if you move between countries.**


One package covering both countries saves buying a second plan when you fly between them.


- **Keep your home line active**


if your home bank sends verification codes by text.


## Does a long stay on the Malaysia DE Rantau visa change the answer?


For payments, a longer stay changes nothing. For daily life, a local number starts to pay for itself. A Penang digital nomad on the Malaysia DE Rantau visa still pays the nasi kandar counter on Chulia Street the same way a two-week visitor does. Where a local number helps is with couriers ringing from your condo lobby. Lazada and Shopee orders also need a local delivery address, which matters more once you have one.


## How do you pay a DuitNow or KHQR code with Moreta Pay?


With connectivity and the right app in place, the payment itself takes five steps.


1. **Top up in your own currency.**


Options are US ACH, SEPA (EUR), UK Faster Payments (GBP), Canadian Interac e-Transfer (CAD), Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover, Apple Pay or Google Pay. USDC/USDT on Solana can fund payments in Malaysia. Stablecoin funding is not enabled for spending in Cambodia, though Moreta Pay still pays KHQR codes when you fund with a card, Apple Pay, Google Pay or a bank transfer.


2. **Get online.**


Use your eSIM or Wi-Fi.


3. **Scan the merchant's code.**


You can also import a saved screenshot of the code.


4. **Check the review screen.**


It shows the merchant name, the amount, the FX rate and the fee.


5. **Slide to confirm.**


The merchant is paid in local currency and you get a receipt.


Moreta reports a single 1.5% fee per payment, shown before you confirm, with no monthly plan. In Malaysia, Moreta lists a maximum of 12,000 MYR per payment and 24,000 MYR per week.


## Where will you still need cash in Malaysia and Cambodia?


QR covers most of your spending, but it does not cover all of it.


- **Malaysia:**


carry a few 10 MYR notes and coins for parking machines, small donations at Kek Lok Si, and the occasional uncle who waves away his own sticker.


- **Cambodia:**


tuk-tuk drivers outside Angkor Wat and stalls in rural Kampot often prefer cash. Change frequently arrives as a mix of US dollars and riel, the two-currency quirk we covered in our Cambodia guide.


- **At ATMs and card terminals:**


decline dynamic currency conversion and always choose to be charged in the local currency.


## What should you set up before landing?


To put all of this into practice, do three things before you board:


1. Install a regional eSIM that covers both countries.


2. Download your payment app and finish passport-and-selfie verification on your home Wi-Fi before you fly, not at a hawker counter.


3. Pull out a modest cash float on arrival, declining any conversion offer at the ATM.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Can I pay a DuitNow QR code with a foreign phone number?


Yes. DuitNow does not check your number. Touch 'n Go eWallet accepts numbers from several supported foreign countries, and Moreta Pay needs no local SIM.


### Does KHQR work without a Cambodian bank account?


Yes. Bakong Tourists lets foreigners register with an email address. Moreta Pay pays KHQR codes from a balance you fund at home.


### Do I need data at the exact moment I pay?


Yes. Moreta Pay needs mobile data or Wi-Fi when you scan and pay. It has no offline mode.


### Can I fund KHQR payments with stablecoins?


No. USDC/USDT funding is not enabled for spending in Cambodia. Use a card, Apple Pay, Google Pay or a bank transfer instead.


### Is Moreta a bank?


No. Moreta Global Inc. is a FinCEN-registered Money Services Business.
